sources.citation: Friesen, Dan T. 2002. Oroko orthography development: Linguistic and sociolinguistic factors. MA thesis, University of North Dakota. 154 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 3.3 'Oroko Phonemes' covers vowels (7-vowel system, no underlying length), consonants and 3.3.3 Tone (pp. 41-44): 'Mbonge is a two-tone system' with floating tones, automatic and non-automatic downstep, H-tone spread; compares Kuperus 1985 on Londo tone (two tones, p.61). The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur in a prosodic sense anywhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Atta, Samuel Ebongkome. 1993. The phonology of Lukundu (Bakundu). Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. v+100 pp.
sources.note: Ch. 4 'Supra-segmental phonology' (p.61ff) treats syllable structure (open-syllable CV language), morpheme/word structure and 4.5 Tones (p.78ff): 'we consider Lukundu (a typical coastal bantu language) as a tonal language. There exists four different types of tones - high, low, rising and falling', plus downdrift (4.5.4). No mention of stress or accent anywhere (scanned text grepped: stress/accent/intonation nil).

sources.citation: Friesen, Lisa. 2002. Valence change and Oroko verb morphology (Mbonge dialect). MA thesis, University of North Dakota. x+124 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Verb Tones' (p.18) lists eight tone facts (two underlying tones H and L, contour tones only on VV, nasals non-syllabic and toneless, downstep, H spread, default L) quoting Friesen, Scott & Scott 2001. Only mention of stress is p.106: 'further study is needed in the areas of animacy, topicalization, tone, stress, and intonation.' No placement statement.
